1.bug_scenario: When drawing circles or other custom geometries with the Draw interaction in useGeographic mode, the shapes are grossly distorted at high latitudes. A "square" drawn as a regular polygon appears skewed and non-regular (first screenshot), and a box drawn via createBox does not match the pointer bounds but instead produces a stretched or mis-positioned rectangle inside the projected circle outline (second screenshot).

2.explanation: The Draw class’s exported geometryFunction generators (createRegularPolygon and createBox) build shapes assuming a flat (projected) coordinate system, so in geographic mode these Euclidean constructions become warped by the map projection at high latitudes. Likewise, the Circle geometry’s setCenterAndRadius (and its reliance on a simple flat-coordinate radius calculation) does not account for geodesic distance, so drawn circles do not actually extend to the pointer. To fix the bug, these functions must be updated to use great-circle or other geodesic computations (for example, via the utilities in ol/geom/flat/geodesic.js) when useGeographic is enabled, ensuring shapes remain true to the user’s pointer on the globe.
2.bug_scenario: When the Draw interaction is used with useGeographic (i.e. geographic coordinates) turned on, shapes that should be perfect circles or regular polygons become distorted—drawn circles often don’t reach the pointer at high latitudes and boxes or polygons created via createBox/createRegularPolygon appear skewed or irregular.
